findings.reason: without one case carrying a marked request line through the host into its child entry, the seam §3 was changed to feed is untested and an implementation can go green while abandoning every run dispatched before a /clear.
findings.text: §5's fifth case supplies the `owner_checked: true` child entry as a previous record written by the test, while nothing asserts the production path that must create it: a request line marked by §3's `_request_host_follower`, parsed by `session_host.parse_request` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:193`), which returns only `(project, session)` and discards the mark, and recorded by `SessionHost.record()` (`:368`), whose child entries carry only project/session/pid/settled_at — an implementation that adds the start-up scan and `waiting_for_dispatch` but never stores the mark passes every case in §3 and §5 while the pre-/clear adoption is dead in production

findings.reason: one bullet, "a hand-off naming the calling session writes one request", closes a hole where the new guard can disable a production delivery path with every declared case green.
findings.text: §3 puts the guard in `_request_host_follower`, the writer both paths share, but its four cases measure only the ask's positive path (case 2) and the hand-off's refusal (case 3), so a guard that also refuses a legitimate hand-off — for instance because `_calling_session()` resolves empty in a follower process rather than in the session's Claude process — passes all four cases while the hand-off silently stops writing its request
